name: Kingston
text: The movement's heartland. After Pinnacle was destroyed, Rastas settled in West Kingston yards such as Back-O-Wall, whose residents were moved out in 1966 to build Tivoli Gardens. The Mansions all have their roots here, and so do the sound systems that carried the message out.

name: New York and Newark
text: An overlooked birthplace of Rasta ideas. The Holy Piby was published in Newark in 1924, and the Ethiopian World Federation was founded in New York in 1937. From the 1970s, large Rasta communities grew in Brooklyn and the Bronx.

name: London and Birmingham
text: Rastafari arrived with the Windrush generation and took hold among young Black Britons in the 1970s, in Brixton, Ladbroke Grove and Handsworth. British reggae from Steel Pulse to Aswad carried it further. In 1993 the Court of Appeal ruled Rastafari were not an ethnic group under race law; protections for religion and belief now give a separate route.

name: Accra
text: Ghana's pan-African history draws Rastas from across the diaspora, and the Rastafari Council of Ghana speaks for a local community. In 2021 the High Court ordered the elite Achimota School to admit two Rasta students it had refused over their locks.

name: Shashamane
text: The promised land made real. Haile Selassie granted 500 acres here in 1948 for diaspora people who had supported Ethiopia. Settlers came from the 1960s, but after Selassie's fall the Derg seized much of the land. In 2017 Ethiopia announced identity cards for Rastafari residents who had lived for decades without citizenship.

name: Knysna and Cape Town
text: Rastafari grew quickly after apartheid, with communities in Cape Town's townships and at Judah Square in Knysna. The Rastafari lawyer Gareth Prince fought for years over cannabis and religious freedom; in 2018 the Constitutional Court allowed private use.

name: Ruātoria
text: On the East Coast of the North Island, young Māori in Ruātoria took up Rastafari in the 1970s and 1980s, weaving it into their own identity and struggles over land. Its influence runs through Māori reggae, from Herbs onwards.

name: Tokyo and Osaka
text: One of the largest reggae scenes outside Jamaica. The Japanese sound system Mighty Crown won the World Clash in 1999, a landmark for the culture. A smaller community practises Rastafari as a faith rather than a sound.

name: São Luís
text: Known as the “Brazilian Jamaica”. São Luís in Maranhão built its own reggae culture around giant radiola sound systems, and Rastafari communities have also grown in Salvador, Bahia.
